advice: Suggestions about what someone should do.
aims: Goals that someone intends to achieve.
ambiguity: The possibility of understanding something in more than one way.
analogy: A comparison that explains a similarity between different things.
annex: An addition to a building or another attached item.
approval: Agreement with something or official permission for it.
assurance: A statement intended to provide confidence or a promise that something will happen.
barter: The exchange of goods or services without money.
beam: To send a signal or energy in a particular direction.
behalf: Representation or benefit, usually in the phrase on behalf of.
bias: An unfair preference for or against a person or group.
bill: A statement of money owed, a banknote, or a proposed law.
bleach: A substance used to remove colour or whiten materials.
blight: A plant disease that causes leaves or other parts to decay.
blink: A very short moment, or a quick closing and opening of the eyes.
bolt: A metal fastener with a threaded shaft, usually secured by a nut.
boot: The storage compartment at the back of a car in British English.
bounty: Generosity or a reward offered for a particular action.
bribe: To offer money or a benefit to influence someone dishonestly.
brink: An edge, or the point just before an event occurs.
bruise: To damage tissue under the skin without breaking the skin.
bud: To begin producing a new shoot or flower.
burning: Producing flames, very hot, or strongly felt.
bustle: Busy and noisy activity, especially involving hurried movement.
carrier: A person or animal that can spread an infection without necessarily showing symptoms.
cast: The actors in a production; to throw or project something.
cell: A basic unit of life, a small enclosed room, or a box in a spreadsheet.
charges: Fees, formal accusations, electrical quantities, or responsibilities.
charm: A quality that makes someone pleasant or attractive to others.
china: Dishes and other objects made of fine ceramic material.
chip: A small electronic component containing a complex circuit.
choice: The act of selecting, or one of the alternatives available.
clash: To conflict, disagree strongly, or strike together.
comfort: A state of physical ease, or relief from worry or sadness.
conditioning: Learning in which an association develops between a stimulus and a response.
contempt: A strong feeling that someone or something deserves no respect.
converse: A statement or relationship that reverses another.
cooker: An appliance used to cook food, especially a stove.
cooks: People who prepare food, especially as their job.
crane: A machine with a long arm that lifts and moves heavy loads.
custody: The legal right and responsibility to care for a child.
dances: Activities involving rhythmic movement, often with music.
dash: A small amount added to food or drink.
default: A setting used automatically unless another option is chosen.
delegate: To give a task or responsibility to another person.
developing: Growing or becoming more advanced; also the present participle of develop.
dip: A decrease, or a brief movement into liquid.
disdain: A feeling that someone or something is not worthy of respect.
double-grill: A cooking grill arranged to heat food on two sides or levels.
drill: A powered tool or machine for making holes.
effort: Physical or mental energy used to achieve something.
esteem: Respect and admiration for a person or thing.
exit: A way out of a building or enclosed area.
experiences: Events someone has lived through, or knowledge gained by doing things.
fan: A device that moves air, or an enthusiastic supporter.
fun: Enjoyment, amusement, or an enjoyable activity.
fuse: To join materials by melting, or combine into a single whole.
fuss: Unnecessary excitement, complaint, or worry about something.
gamble: A risky decision or activity with an uncertain result.
glamour: An attractive and exciting quality associated with special people or things.
glance: A quick look at someone or something.
glare: Light that is unpleasantly bright and makes seeing difficult.
grin: A broad smile that usually shows the teeth.
groom: To clean and brush an animal's coat.
handout: Printed information given to a class or group.
iceland: An island country in the North Atlantic Ocean.
icon: A person widely admired as a representative of a culture or activity.
implant: An object or material placed inside the body.
inability: A lack of the skill, strength, or means needed to do something.
insight: A clear and deep understanding of a situation.
insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
jam: A sweet spread made by cooking fruit with sugar.
kindle: To start a fire or cause a feeling to begin.
kiss: A touch with the lips expressing affection or greeting.
learned: Having much knowledge, or the past form of learn.
lever: To lift or move something using a rigid bar as a lever.
liability: A legal responsibility, a financial debt, or an obligation.
lime: A white calcium-containing material used in building and to treat acidic soil.
living room: A room in a home where people sit and spend time together.
log: A cut section of a tree, or a written record of a journey or activity.
majesty: Great dignity, authority, or impressive grandeur.
marked: Clearly noticeable; also the past form of mark.
mastery: Thorough knowledge of or great skill in something.
mate: To breed by joining sexually or by bringing animals together for breeding.
may: The fifth month of the year.
meaningless: Having no clear meaning, purpose, or value.
menace: A person or thing likely to cause danger or serious trouble.
mercy: Kindness that reduces punishment or suffering.
mission: An important task or purpose that someone is sent or expected to carry out.
mistake: An incorrect action, judgement, or result.
mole: A small burrowing mammal with strong front feet.
monitor: To check and track something over time.
mop: A thick, untidy mass of hair.
navy: The military force that operates a country's warships.
neglect: A failure to provide the attention or care that is needed.
niggle: A small complaint or persistent minor concern.
nuts: Hard-shelled fruits with an edible seed inside.
organ: A body part that performs a particular function, such as the heart or liver.
overload: An amount of work or weight that exceeds capacity.
overuse: Use that is excessive or too frequent.
palm: A tropical tree with a long trunk and large leaves near the top.
perk: An extra benefit received from a job or position.
permission: Approval that allows someone to do something.
pinch: A squeeze between two surfaces, or a very small amount.
pitch: The height of a sound, a sports field, or to put up a tent.
pity: Sadness and concern for another person's suffering.
plant: A living organism that usually grows in soil; also a factory or industrial facility.
plate: A flat dish used for serving food.
plays: Dramatic works written to be performed by actors.
plot: The events of a story, a small area of land, or to mark data on a graph.
plumb: A weight suspended on a line to show a vertical direction.
pound: A unit of British currency, divided into one hundred pence.
presents: Things given to someone as gifts.
pretension: A claim to importance or ability that may be unjustified.
price: The money required to buy something, or the cost of obtaining it.
proceeding: Continuing or moving forward with an activity.
proficiency: A high level of skill or ability.
prominence: The state of being noticeable or important.
raid: To attack a place suddenly or search it with official authority.
rash: A sudden large number of similar events, often unpleasant.
recourse: Help or a course of action used in a difficult situation.
reform: A change intended to improve a system or practice.
relapse: A return to an illness or an earlier unwanted condition or behaviour.
remit: The range of matters a person or organization is responsible for.
reservations: Bookings made in advance, or doubts about a proposal.
responsibility: A duty to take care of something or answer for an action.
revolution: A major change in a political system or in the way something is done.
ridicule: Unkind laughter or remarks intended to make someone seem foolish.
rivals: People or groups competing for the same goal.
root: The part of a plant that takes in water, or the basic cause of something.
safeguard: To protect someone or something from harm.
sake: Purpose or benefit, usually in the phrase for the sake of.
saw: The past tense of see, meaning noticed or observed with the eyes.
scoop: To lift or remove something with a spoon-like movement.
scramble: A hurried competition to obtain something.
scrub: An area of low bushes and small woody plants.
seal: To close an opening so that air, liquid, or other material cannot pass through.
service: Help or work provided to others; to inspect and maintain equipment.
set up: To establish, organize, or put something into position.
shriek: A short, high, very loud cry.
signature: A person's name written in their own distinctive way.
ski: To move over snow using long narrow boards attached to the feet.
specialty: A food for which a restaurant or region is especially known.
spite: A desire to upset or hurt someone.
splash: A mark made by scattered liquid, or a noticeable effect.
sprawl: Unplanned or irregular expansion over a wide area.
sprint: A short race or burst of running at high speed.
spy: To secretly observe people or collect information about them.
stern: The rear part of a ship or boat.
stumble: A brief loss of balance while walking or running.
sue: To bring a legal claim against a person or organization.
supports: Structures that hold something up or keep it in place.
sympathy: Concern for someone experiencing trouble or suffering.
talent: A natural ability to do something well.
temptation: A desire to do or have something that may be unwise or wrong.
tender: Soft enough to cut or chew easily.
tenor: The overall meaning or direction of a statement.
thrust: The force that pushes something forward.
tie: To fasten with a cord or knot, restrict, or finish with an equal score.
tint: To add a small amount of colour to something.
tire: To make someone feel less energetic or in need of rest.
tires: Makes someone feel less energetic or in need of rest.
toast: Bread that has been browned by heat.
trains: Connected railway vehicles that carry passengers or goods.
trunk: A tree's main stem, a large travel case, or an elephant's long nose.
twist: A turning movement, a bend, or an unexpected change.
tyre: The rubber covering fitted around a vehicle wheel.
void: An empty space or a gap left by something absent.
whirlwind: A situation involving a great deal of rapid and busy activity.
wrong: Incorrect, unsuitable, or unjust; also an unjust act.
